headline: Bathinda Records 23 Stubble Fires as PM2.5 Forecast Reaches 102.3
briefing: On 2025-10-31, Bathinda district recorded 23 fire detections with a total fire radiative power of 108.2 MW, ranking 3 among Punjab districts out of a total of 273 detections. This represents a 151.6% increase compared to its 7-day mean of 9.1 detections. In the 2024 season, Bathinda recorded 658 fire detections [K092]. Bathinda recorded a PM2.5 level of 105.6 today. For tomorrow, the PM2.5 forecast p50 is 102.3, with an 80% forecast uncertainty band from p10 of 61.8 to p90 of 131.2. Winds are blowing FROM the NNW at 6.8 km/h. As context, upwind fire pressure stands at 715.8, with Outside Punjab contributing 64.1%, Tarn Taran 13.0%, and Ferozepur 5.9%. A key limitation is that satellite fire counts are a lower bound because satellites miss fires under cloud cover or between overpasses [K035].

The busiest day was 2024-11-17, with 93 detections.

Compared with the previous season: -75% compared with 2023 (2,615 detections).

results.title: Limitations of this project
results.text:
# What to keep in mind when reading any output

**Fires.** Satellites detect heat anomalies. They do not know that a fire is stubble burning. They miss fires that burn between overpasses, fires under cloud, and small or short burns. A district's detection count is a lower bound. Fire dates are UTC dates that we treat as local days, so some night detections are filed one day early.

**Air quality.** PM2.5 is modelled by CAMS on a coarse grid. It is not measured at street level and it is not CPCB monitor data. It already includes fire emissions as the model sees them.

**Districts.** We use 22 district boundaries. Malerkotla, created in 2021, is not a separate district in our boundary data. Its area is counted in Sangrur.
